label: LaMancha

names.text: The article gives Lamancha, LaMancha and American Lamancha as names, and says that at registration in 1958 it was listed as 'Lamancha or American Lamancha'. Read with WebFetch.

about.text: An American short-eared dairy goat, first bred in California around 1927 by Eula Fay Frey and later developed at Glide, Oregon. Its milk averaged about 3.9% fat and 3.1% protein in ADGA's 2010 lactation averages.

sources.text: Wikipedia article read with WebFetch for the breeding history in California and Oregon. The Purdue factsheet read with WebFetch for the ADGA 2010 averages of fat and protein.

origin.place: Glide, Oregon, USA; first bred in California by Eula Fay Frey around 1927

sources.text: Wikipedia, read with WebFetch: first bred in California by Mrs. Eula Fay Frey about 1927, moved to Glide, Oregon; formally registered on 27 January 1958. The 1927 to 1958 range runs from first breeding to registration. Purdue says it originated in Oregon from crosses of short-eared goats with Nubians, which conflicts with Wikipedia's account of its ancestry.

Purdue factsheet, read with WebFetch: 'ADGA Production Averages (2010 lactations)': 2,246 lbs of milk per lactation. Converted at 0.4536 kg per lb to 1,019 kg, so estimated. Lactation length not stated on the page.
Purdue factsheet, read with WebFetch: ADGA 2010 lactation averages, fat 3.9%, protein 3.1%.

facts.v: Fay's Spider L-85 in 1961 was the first LaMancha doe to pass 3,000 lb on an official test, with 3,295 lb of milk in 305 days. That record stood for twelve years.

sources.text: Wikipedia, read with WebFetch: 'Fay's Spider L-85 became the first Lamancha doe to exceed 3000 pounds on an official test, with 305-day figures of 3295 and 115.8. The record stood for twelve years.' The article does not label the units, and pounds are taken from its 3000 pounds wording.

facts.v: Frey's goal was 3½ to six quarts of fine-flavored milk with 3.5% or more butterfat per period of one to four years between freshenings.

sources.text: Wikipedia, read with WebFetch: Frey's breeding goal, quoted as '3½ to six quarts of fine-flavored milk with 3.5% or more butterfat'.

gaps: No DAD-IS population figure or risk status found, and the Wikipedia article gives no conservation status. The original-stock count conflicts within the article (about 200 at registration, and 130 in the foundation herd), so it is left out. The origin accounts conflict on ancestry (Wikipedia: short-eared Spanish goats; Purdue: short-eared goats crossed with Nubians). The ADGA average has no lactation length. Purposes are left out because no opened page stated them. The yield is the only ADGA figure found; the 2100 lb figures from search text were not used.
